1. Heard the parties.

This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding arising out of Raneshwar P.S. Case No. 44 of 2020 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 266 of 2022 including the order taking cognizance dated 07.04.2022 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Dumka whereby and where under the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the offences ( 2025:JHHC:24686 ) punishable under Section 498A/323/341/34 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text: The allegation against the petitioners is that the petitioner no. 1 being the husband of the informant and the petitioner nos. 2 to 4 being the relatives of the petitioner no.1 treated the informant with cruelty in connection with demand of dowry of a Scooty and assaulted her and wrongfully restrained her in furtherance of their common intention.

Basing upon the written report submitted by the informant,
police registered Raneshwar P.S. Case No. 44 of 2020 and took up investigation of the case.

After completion of investigation, police submitted charge sheet against the petitioners for having committed the offences and found the allegations against the petitioners to be true and basing upon the same, the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the said offences.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the allegations against the petitioners are all false and the petitioners are still ready and willing to keep the informant with proper dignity.
The petitioner no.1 has filed a case under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal right.
It is next submitted that the allegations against the petitioners are general and omnibus in nature.
It is further submitted that the petitioner no.1 was not present at his residence on the alleged date of occurrence.
Mahila Police Station issued a notice to both the parties fixing 05.08.2020 for conciliation but the same failed.

It is (
2025:JHHC:24686 ) further submitted that the father of the informant made an application before the Officer-in-Charge of Chowringhee Police Out Post on 08.07.2020 for intimating that he is taking the informant with him and the informant has given in writing that she is also leaving her matrimonial house willingly.
Hence, it is submitted that the prayer as prayed for by the petitioners in this criminal miscellaneous petition be allowed.

5. The learned Special Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer as prayed for by the petitioners in this criminal miscellaneous petition and submits that the defence sought to be adduced by the petitioners is false and fabricated.

It is next submitted that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioners of harassing the informant with a view to coerce her to meet the unlawful dowry demand of Scooty and the harassment was made by assaulting her and also taking her stree dhan properties.
It is then submitted that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioners of demand of dowry.

Hence, it is submitted that if the allegations made against the petitioners in the F.I.R. are considered to be true in their entirety, then all the offences in respect of which cognizance has been taken against the petitioners is made out against the petitioners.
Hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials available in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Sutanu Barat vs The State Of Jharkhand on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68255159/
2 India in the case of Harjinder Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Another, reported in 2025 SCC Online SC 1029, para -11 of which reads as under:-
"11.

sentences.text: The primary argument of Respondent no. 2 rests on his alibi.

An alibi, however,
is a plea in the nature of a defence; the burden to establish it rests squarely on the accused.

Here, the documents relied upon, parking chit, chemist's receipt, OPD card,
CCTV clip, have yet to be formally proved.
Until that exercise is undertaken, they remain untested pieces of paper.

To treat them as conclusive at the threshold would invert the established order of criminal proceedings, requiring the Court to pronounce upon a defence before the prosecution is allowed to lead its full evidence.
Even assuming the documents will eventually be proved, their face value does not eclipse the prosecution version.
The parking slip is timed at 06:30 a.m.; the chemist's bill and CCTV images are from 12:09 p.m.
The confrontation is alleged at 08:30 a.m.
A road journey from Jagowal to Chandigarh of roughly ninety kilometres in a private vehicle can comfortably be accomplished within the intervening window.
More importantly, abetment to suicide is not an offence committed at a single moment.

It may consist of a build-up of psychological pressure culminating in self- destruction,
and the law punishes that build-up wherever and whenever it occurs."
( Emphasis Supplied)

the defence of the petitioner that the petitioner no.1 was not residing at his residence or for that matter some documents of some police station apparently obtained under the provisions of the Right to Information Act are the defences the burden to establish of which squarely rests upon the accused person.
The documents relied upon by the petitioner to quash the entire criminal proceeding is to be proved during the trial of the case.
Until that exercise is undertaken such favour certainly remains ( 2025:JHHC:24686 ) untested being a mere piece of a paper.

To treat such document as conclusive at the threshold would involve the established order of criminal proceeding requiring the court to pronounce upon a defence before the prosecution version is brought on record.

7. Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that it is a settled principle of law that no mini trial can be conducted by a High Court in exercise of its power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. vs. Akhil Sharda & Ors. reported in 2022 LiveLaw SC 594, the relevant portion of which reads as under:-
" Having gone through the impugned judgment and order passed by the High court has set aside the criminal proceedings in exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC

entities.text: State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. vs. Akhil Sharda & Ors. reported in 2022 LiveLaw SC 594
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
,
it appears that the High Court has virtually conducted a mini trial, which as such is not permissible at this stage and while deciding the application under Section 482CrPC.

As observed and held by this court in a catena of decisions, no mini trial can be conducted by the High Court in exercise of power under Section 482CrPC,
jurisdiction and at the stage of deciding the application under Section 482CrPC, the High Court cannot get into appreciation of evidence of the particular case being considering.
(Emphasis supplied)

3 8.

sentences.text:
Under such circumstances and considering the fact that if the allegations made in the F.I.R. and the materials collected during the investigation of the case are considered to be true in their entirety, the offences in respect of which the cognizance has been taken is made out against the petitioners. Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that this is a not a fit case where the entire criminal proceeding including the order taking cognizance dated 07.04.2025, passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, ( 2025:JHHC:24686 ) Dumka in connection with Raneshwar P.S. Case No. 44 of 2020 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 266 of 2022 is to be quashed basing upon the defence of the petitioners.
9.
Accordingly, this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit is dismissed.
